question: Why do many physicists find Many-Worlds cleaner than the Copenhagen interpretation?
answer: Copenhagen adds a special collapse rule that stops the wave at every measurement. Many-Worlds keeps only the Schrödinger equation: the wave branches, and you see the branch you are entangled with. The experience is the same, but the maths is cleaner.
move: Many-Worlds drops collapse: wave functions just follow one equation.

web.label: A hand-drawn tree: a wave grows up from its source, forking at three measurements, you at the top. At its foot two rule cards: the Schrödinger equation, and collapse with scissors that cut every branch but yours. The reader flips to Many-Worlds: the collapse card falls away and every branch grows on, with other yous at the tips. Asks why physicists find Many-Worlds cleaner.

source: Veritasium, “Why Parallel Universes Are Probably Real” (YouTube, 2020)
